newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Three Moslems injured in bus stoning in Brcko - UN.
newsitem.headline: Three Moslems injured in bus stoning in Brcko - UN.

text.p: Three Moslems travelling in a bus to visit the disputed Bosnian town of Brcko were hurt by stones on Thursday, U.N. spokeswoman Andrea Angeli said.
Two buses carrying about 80 people had left from the Moslem-Croat federation territory to visit the Serb-controlled river port.
"Well inside Serb territory, someone threw stones and smashed windows on one bus, injuring three people," Angeli said.
Brcko on the river Sava links the eastern and western halves of Serb-held territory in Bosnia. The Serbs seized it early in the 1992-95 war and purged its Moslem-Croat population.
The two buses were to be the first in a series of visits arranged by a U.N. supervisor for former Brcko residents.
"We condemn the stoning in the strongest possible words," a spokesman for the supervisor's office said. "It is very important that we maintain the principle (of freedom of movement).
The buses made their way to the supervisor's office in the centre of town, Angeli said. While the Moslem group was inside the building, about 100 Serbs gathered outside and shouted insults.

"On the way back the buses were stoned again, but I don't know whether anybody was injured or there was any damage," Angeli said, adding that local Serb police who escorted the buses did nothing to prevent the crowd from throwing stones.
